shabad.source_english: Codes of Conduct and Other Panthic Sources

en.bdb: Dohra.

verses.gurmukhi: ਪ੍ਰਾਤਹ ਉਠ ਇਸਨਾਨ ਕਰਿ ਪੜਹਿ ਜਾਪੁ ਜਪੁ ਦੋਇ॥
verses.translit_en: praateh uTh isanaan kar paReh jaap jap dhoi||

en.bdb: Arise at the last quarter of night, bathe and then start the morning prayers by reading both Japji and Jaap,

verses.gurmukhi: ਸੋਦਰ ਕੀ ਚੌਂਕੀ ਕਰੇ ਆਲਸ ਕਰੈ ਨ ਕੋਇ॥੪੫॥
verses.translit_en: sodhar kee chaua(n)kee kare aalas karai na koi||45||

en.bdb: Recite the Sodar at evening, do not be lazy about this.
When the first quarter of night arrives;
Recite the Sohila then.
The Bani enshrined in both Granths;

verses.gurmukhi: ਚੁਨ ਚੁਨ ਕੰਠ ਕਰੇ ਨਿਤ ਸੋਈ॥੪੭॥
verses.translit_en: chun chun ka(n)Th kare nit soiee||47||

en.bdb: Select portions from each and commit them to memory.
Days associated with the Gurus, from the tenth to the first;
Celebrate them as festivals and holy days.
Prepare food on these occasions.
Cook the food in an iron bowl and offer it to the Khalsa.
Give as much as you can afford when offering Ardas.
Never come with an empty hand.
A Singh who is a ruler;
He should care for the poorer Singhs.
Show love for the poorer Khalsas.
Increase love for them by giving them horses, and benefactions.
When one finds Singhs who come from afar;
He must serve them whole-heartedly.

verses.gurmukhi: ਭਾਉ ਧਨ ਦੇ ਬਿਦਾ ਸੋ ਕਰੇ॥
verses.translit_en: bhaau dhan dhe bidhaa so kare||

en.bdb: He who bids farewell by bestowing affection and offerings;

verses.gurmukhi: ਰਹੇ ਪਾਸ ਤੇ ਤੋ ਨਿਤ ਅਨੁਸਰੇ॥੫੪॥
verses.translit_en: rahe paas te to nit anusare||54||

en.bdb: Will forever retain his benefactions.
Speak sweetly in the presence of all;
Keep only Singhs as close servants.

verses.gurmukhi: ਸਿੰਘ ਸਿੰਘ ਸੋਂ ਨੇਹੁ ਸੁ ਕਰਨੋ॥
verses.translit_en: si(n)gh si(n)gh so(n) nehu su karano||

en.bdb: A Singh must always have love for other Singhs;
and must banish enmity from his heart.

verses.gurmukhi: ਸਿੰਘ ਸਿੰਘ ਪਰ ਸ਼ਸਤ੍ਰ ਨ ਕਰੇ॥
verses.translit_en: si(n)gh si(n)gh par shasatr na kare||

en.bdb: A Singh must never raise a weapon against another Singh;
See him as the Guru and fear the Khalsa.
